groups.sentence: Instructors align their AI policy and permitted AI use with course learning objectives, without compromising them.
Instructors start from course learning objectives and outcomes, and reassess them, when deciding whether and how to allow AI.
Appropriate AI use depends on the course's learning objectives, since AI can help some goals and hinder others.
Instructors weigh whether AI would support or hinder student learning in each course, task or assignment.
Instructors identify the skills and knowledge students must practice or demonstrate without AI.
Departments, programs and institutions jointly review and state learning outcomes in light of AI.
Instructors tailor AI policies to their discipline and local course context.
Instructors explain to students how the course's AI rules connect to the learning objectives.
Syllabus statements tell students the AI policy exists to protect and promote their learning and the course's goals.
Students must not use AI in ways that bypass or undermine the course's learning objectives.
Students consider whether AI use is appropriate for their learning goals and justify it by relevance to them.
Students may use AI tools when the use aligns with or complements the course learning outcomes.
Instructors return to and evaluate their AI policy and use over time.
